showcase.title: The arcade
showcase.lacks: The arcade lacks a focal point that ties its shops together. Repeated dark brick and similar openings make the storefronts run together.
showcase.fix: Install a tall, warmly lit freestanding clock in the concourse where shoppers can see it from several storefronts.

showcase.title: The Aldermack
showcase.lacks: The lobby lacks a dominant architectural feature that tells visitors where the show is. Small signs carry that information against walls of equally busy ornament.
showcase.fix: Turn a stretch of patterned wall into a recessed auditorium entrance with a lit marquee visible across the lobby.

showcase.title: The avenue
showcase.called: Lamplit city streets under red skies
showcase.lacks: The junction lacks a landmark at street level. Repeated façades and evenly spaced lamps give the eye few clues about where to look or go.
showcase.fix: Give the low stone building a lit entrance facing the fork, with a distinctive marquee visible from both approaches.

showcase.title: The booking hall
showcase.lacks: The hall lacks a recognizable service point. The benches show where to wait, but the room gives arriving travelers no obvious destination.
showcase.fix: Build a recessed, warmly lit ticket window beneath the arrivals and departures board.

showcase.title: St Gallow's
showcase.lacks: The church lacks a recognizable entrance. The small wooden door gets lost at the foot of the tower, leaving the repeated windows to carry the whole facade.
showcase.fix: Rebuild the doorway as a recessed pointed-arch stone portal that gives the tower a recognizable entrance from the street.

showcase.title: The churchyard
showcase.lacks: The churchyard has no visible graves or memorials. The path leads to a tree against a wall, leaving little to distinguish the yard from an empty garden.
showcase.fix: Add a small burial plot at the end of the dirt path, with a tall weathered headstone visible from the entrance.

showcase.title: The crypt
showcase.lacks: The crypt lacks a sense of ceremony. The low, flat ceiling and repeating reliefs make the sarcophagus feel like furniture.
showcase.fix: Raise a ribbed stone vault directly over the sarcophagus so the room’s architecture draws the eye to the tomb.

showcase.title: The harbour
showcase.called: City harbour with a cargo barge
showcase.lacks: The harbour lacks a distinctive vessel silhouette. The barge’s straight sides and flat deck make it easy to mistake for another pier.
showcase.fix: Reshape the existing barge with a tapered bow and a raised stern so its outline reads as a vessel from across the quay.

showcase.title: The pump station
showcase.lacks: A recognizable piece of machinery that connects the sludge vats to the controls and shows what the hall does.
showcase.fix: Install a large sludge filter above the vats, with exposed pipes that visibly feed into them.

showcase.title: The market hall
showcase.lacks: The hall lacks an architectural focal point. The flat ceiling and repeated shelves make its distinctive butcher’s counter feel incidental.
showcase.fix: Build a timber-framed canopy over the butcher’s counter to give the hanging cuts a distinct stall and the hall a recognizable centerpiece.

showcase.title: Welcome to Gravesend
showcase.lacks: The streets lack a clear destination. Repeated windows and dark storefronts give the square little identity beyond the fountain.
showcase.fix: Build a lantern-lit cemetery gate at the far end of the street to give the square a destination tied to the Gravesend sign.

showcase.title: St Gallow's nave
showcase.lacks: A clear processional aisle. The unbroken pew rows push circulation to the walls and interrupt the sightline from the back of the nave to the altar.
showcase.fix: Split the pew rows down the middle to create a continuous aisle leading straight to the altar steps.

showcase.title: The pawn shop
showcase.lacks: The pawn counter has little visual pull. The flat lighting gives the merchandise, checkerboard floor, and back door nearly equal weight.
showcase.fix: Add a warm pool of light over the pawn counter so the goods and transaction area draw the eye from the street.

showcase.title: The platform and the train
showcase.lacks: A clear boarding point. The waiting-room doors blend into the long brick wall, leaving the platform without a focal point.
showcase.fix: Install a lit canopy over the waiting-room doors, casting light across the boarding strip and onto the carriage.

showcase.title: RAT DOGS
showcase.lacks: A recognizable cooking station. The rats and cleaver tell us what gets prepped, but the room gives that joke nowhere to go.
showcase.fix: Install a lit industrial griddle against the back wall, with a row of rats sizzling beneath its hood.

showcase.title: The saloon
showcase.lacks: The counters, tables and walls blend into the same dark wood tones. The saloon lacks a focal point that makes it clear where drinks are served.
showcase.fix: Build a warmly lit backbar with tiered bottle shelves behind the main counter.

showcase.title: The sewers
showcase.lacks: The sewer lacks a spatial focal point. The same low ceiling and wall panels repeat, and the channel has no visible destination.
showcase.fix: Turn one junction into a tall outfall chamber where the channel drops into a catch basin.

showcase.title: Gravesend Station
showcase.lacks: The street has no visible sign of railway activity beyond the name and clock. The dark arches give arriving players little sense of where to go.
showcase.fix: Turn the main entrance into a lit ticket hall with a ticket window and departure board visible from the street.

showcase.title: The unfinished metro
showcase.lacks: The junction lacks a strong focal point. The ticket grille and signs suggest a station, but the booth blends into the masonry.
showcase.fix: Rebuild the barred recess as a warmly lit ticket booth with a service counter visible from the foot of the stairs.

showcase.title: The works yard
showcase.lacks: The courtyard lacks a strong focal point. The serving hatch is its most distinctive feature, yet it reads as another opening in a wall of repeating windows.
showcase.fix: Extend the Rat Dogs serving hatch into the courtyard as a roofed service counter that the tables can cluster around.
